subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB964 + PB1027. The omitted ADVANCING phrase acts as AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE (GR25), and PB1027 makes that LITERAL: SequentialConnector.WriteRecord reroutes it to WriteAdvancingRecord(lines: 1, before: false) in EVERY state of the device, for record sequential and line sequential files alike, so the two spellings are one path and write the same file byte for byte (PlainWriteAdvancingConformanceTests holds every three-write mix of plain/AFTER/BEFORE, with and without LINAGE). Before PB1027 it took BEFORE's placement (record, then its line end) whenever no line was open: no blank line after a BEFORE write, the first record of a LINAGE page one line high, a line sequential file travelling twice around an AFTER write. a) n lines = n line terminators; c) zero = a bare carriage return on an open line (overprint; R54); d) mnemonic = implementor-defined zero-line advance, the record always released; e)/f) BEFORE presents then advances, AFTER advances then presents; g) PAGE on a LINAGE file repositions to the next logical page; h) PAGE with no LINAGE = a form feed. Determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4, Annex A.3 item 37): a file supports vertical positioning when its description has a LINAGE clause or once an ADVANCING phrase has been written to it (SequentialConnector.SupportsVerticalPositioning); a file of which neither holds (an ordinary text or fixed-block data file written with plain WRITEs only) has nothing to position, so its plain WRITE is the record and its line end, with no leading empty line - the GnuCOBOL 3.2 default; the earlier note 'every sequential file supports vertical positioning' is withdrawn. b) (negative identifier) is undefined. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#EmitLineSequentialRecord (kb/Work PB1027 deleted both: a plain WRITE on a file that supports vertical positioning is the explicit AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE path (WriteAdvancingRecord), so there is no placement question left to ask and no separate line sequential arm) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#ImplicitAdvanceIsBefore (kb/Work PB1027 deleted both: a plain WRITE on a file that supports vertical positioning is the explicit AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE path (WriteAdvancingRecord), so there is no placement question left to ask and no separate line sequential arm)
